caption: Nobody warns you that a funeral has a monthly instalment. How long did yours take to pay off?

slides.title:
How I spend
my R29 000
p/m salary
Living in Phalaborwa
slides.body:
Female, 35
Single, supporting her mother
Job: Mine plant administrator
Net salary: R29 000 p/m

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: Feeding four people now instead of one
slides.body: Nobody tells you a death changes your grocery bill too.

slides.title: Rent
slides.includes: 2 bed near the mine, my mother stays with me now
slides.body: She moved in after the funeral. I haven't had the heart to bring up rent.

slides.title: Funeral loan repayment
slides.includes: Catering, tent hire and the coffin, split over 18 months
slides.body: My father died in April. This is the one that still catches me some months.

slides.title: Black tax
slides.includes: My two younger siblings' school fees, since my father can't anymore
slides.body: I didn't exactly choose this. I'm just the one with a job.

slides.title: Car instalment
slides.includes: The Etios I financed the month before he passed
slides.body: Bad timing. I don't regret it, I just felt it.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Medical aid, a second funeral policy for the rest of us, electricity, cellphone, stokvel, transport
slides.body: I took out my own funeral policy the week after his. I'm not doing this twice unprepared.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R29 000. Grief has a monthly instalment plan now, same as everything else.

slides.title: I needed to see the whole picture
slides.body:
I uploaded my statements to Beyond Horizon once the loan repayments started, just to know I could still cover everything.

Seeing it laid out made the eighteen months feel possible instead of endless.

No bank login needed.
